conviction_note: Q1 (Jun-Aug) all-store sales came in at 93.3% of last year on Honeys' own 月次. The H1 plan was built on 既存店 99.1%, and running that sales shortfall through the plan's own gross-margin and SG&A lines puts Q1 operating profit at roughly ¥0.3-0.7bn against ¥1.2bn last year, about 20% of the ¥2.2bn H1 guide against the usual 37-44%. That is a reported-quarter negative sized at -1.5, not larger, because the sales half has been public since 2 September. This holder base also posted 0.00% close-to-close on a similarly 月次-foreshadowed OP collapse in Q3 FY26, and opening dips on this name have been bought back twice.
bar: The company's own H1 FY2027/5 guide, operating profit ¥2,200m (sales ¥28,700m, gross margin plan 58.0%, SG&A ¥14,450m), from the 2026-07-07 決算短信 (https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/library/detail/376?attach=true&fld=file&browserview=true) and 決算説明会資料 p20 (https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/library/detail/378?attach=true&fld=file&browserview=true). No sell-side consensus exists: kabuyoho shows no analyst estimate (https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=2792). Q1's share of H1 OP was 44% in FY26 (1,205/2,733) and 37% in FY25 (1,233/3,295), per kabutan (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=2792). That makes the guide-implied Q1 about ¥810-970m, midpoint ~¥890m. My estimate is ~¥450m (range 250-700), which gives print_vs_bar of about -45% on operating profit. On sales the gap is ~-6.5%: ~¥12.9bn against a ~¥13.8bn guide-pace Q1. The OP estimate is my arithmetic from the company's own numbers, not a sourced figure.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% with no disclosed seller at or above 0.5% (baseline, as of 2026-09-18, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html), so there is no crowded short to squeeze against a negative. Margin (kabutan 信用残, https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=2792&ashi=shin, week of 2026-09-25): margin longs rose from 73,700 shares (09-04) to 133,100 (09-25), up 81% in three weeks, while margin shorts held flat at 76-79k. That puts 信用倍率 at 1.68, up from 0.88. Retail is buying the dip into the print, not leaning short. The May margin-short spike (843k shares) was a 優待 cross around the May record date, not directional. There is no skew because there are no single-stock options.

findings.finding: Honeys' own 月次 puts Q1 (Jun-Aug 2026) all-store sales at 93.3% and 既存店 at 93.5% of last year (June 84.4%, July 100.8%, August 95.1%). The H1 plan assumed 既存店 99.1% and a 58.0% gross margin, so Q1 operating profit should come in near ¥0.45bn (range 0.25-0.7) against ¥1.21bn last year: about 20% progress on the ¥2.2bn H1 guide against 37-44% in the last two years.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Close-to-close after the known release dates (Yahoo 3y bars; kabutan 発表日). Q1 FY26 (2025-09-29), sales -2.9% with OP -2% cushioned by a +2.5pt gross margin: +0.52% (open +1.82%). Q1 FY25 (2024-09-26): +2.80% after opening -2.09%. The closest analog is Q3 FY26 (2026-03-26), where sales fell 4.8%, as visible in 月次, and OP swung from -94 to -505: 0.00% (open -0.55%). Negative guide prints did move the stock: H1 FY26 -2.95%, FY26 -2.19%, FY25 -5.77%.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-02 (August 月次; June posted 2026-07-02, July 2026-08-04, per https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/news)
findings.why_not_priced: The sales half is public and is priced. The stock has held 1,400-1,470 since the June 月次 and fell only -1.10% on the August 月次. What is not visible anywhere is the profit arithmetic. No analyst covers the name (kabuyoho shows no consensus), no preview exists, and the company never revises at Q1: kabutan's revision history shows 修 only in January/March/June. So nothing has put a number on a ~60% OP decline or a ~20% progress rate until kabutan's automated 進捗率 headline tomorrow. If it were priced, the stock would sit at or below its June low of 1,315 rather than 7% above it. Retail margin longs would not have risen 81% in the three weeks before the print. Last year's Q1 OP was cushioned by a +2.5pt gross-margin gain, and the plan now calls for a -0.7pt full-year decline, so that cushion is gone this time.
findings.independence: The plan assumptions (既存店 99.1% H1, GM 58.2% FY, H1 OP ¥2,200m) come from a different document, the 2026-07-07 決算説明会資料 (https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/library/detail/378?attach=true&fld=file&browserview=true). The last-year Q1 base (sales 13,899, GM 59.6%, SG&A 7,077, OP 1,205) is from the Q1 FY26 決算短信 (https://www.honeys.co.jp/ir/library/detail/359?attach=true&fld=file&browserview=true). The retail margin build is from kabutan 信用残 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/kabuka?code=2792&ashi=shin). Each is one input to a single calculation, not separate confirmation of the conclusion.

outside_window.finding: September 2026 月次 lands in the first days of October, as August's did on 09-02. Q2 needs roughly 既存店 104% to rescue the H1 plan after Q1's 93.5%, and that release, or a January H1 revision, is where a guidance cut would show. Neither is visible in this window unless the company revises alongside Q1, which it has not done in at least four years.

baseline_tension: The finding agrees with the mildly negative run-up (-4.09% over 20 days) and cuts slightly against the baseline's small positive lean (+0.09). The lean is mostly the run-up term, and nothing in the positioning resists a negative: no disclosed shorts, and margin longs building. Most of the fundamental gap, though, is a public sales series this holder base has repeatedly looked through, so the reaction is sized at about two thirds of the 2.34% event proxy rather than at the size of the OP miss.
